steps.body: Area filled the inside; **perimeter walks the edge.** It's the total distance all the way around a shape — the length of fence it would take to enclose it. To find it, walk every side and add the lengths as you go.
Walk every side of the rectangle.

widget.prompt: Tap all FOUR sides of this rectangle — the ones you must walk to get all the way around.
widget.missFeedback: The fence goes ALL the way around — a rectangle has four sides to walk, not two.
widget.successFeedback: Four sides: 8 + 3 + 8 + 3. A rectangle has two lengths AND two widths — walk them all.

predict.prompt: Walking all the way around this 8-by-3 rectangle — how many times does each measurement get walked?

options.label: The 8 and the 3 each get walked twice

predict.reveal: A rectangle has two matching pairs — going around walks the 8 twice and the 3 twice. That doubling is what perimeter means.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents perimeter.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for perimeter must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines perimeter.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: A rectangle has two 8s and two 3s: 8 + 3 + 8 + 3 = 22 cm of fence.
Shortcut: (8 + 3) = 11, doubled, because the sides come in matching pairs — 22 cm.

widget.prompt: A rectangle is 8 cm long and 3 cm wide. What is its perimeter?

commonErrors.feedback: 11 walked only TWO sides (8 + 3). The fence goes all the way around — two 8s and two 3s: 22.
24 is 8 × 3 — that's the AREA, the squares inside. Perimeter walks the fence: add all four sides.

steps.body: A square makes it even easier: **all four sides match, so perimeter = 4 × side.** A square with 7 cm sides has a fence of 4 × 7 = 28 cm. One multiplication does the whole walk.

explanationVariants: Four equal sides of 7: 4 × 7 = 28 cm around.
Every side is the same, so the walk is just 7 four times: 28 cm.

widget.prompt: A square has sides of 7 cm. What is its perimeter?

commonErrors.feedback: 14 walked only two sides. A square's fence has FOUR equal stretches: 7 × 4 = 28.
49 is 7 × 7 — the AREA inside the square. The fence AROUND adds the four 7-cm sides: 28.

widget.prompt: Sort each real-life job: does it need PERIMETER (the edge) or AREA (the inside)?

items.label: Fencing around a yard
items.feedback: Fence follows the edge — that's perimeter.

items.label: Carpet to cover a floor
items.feedback: Carpet fills the inside — that's area.

items.label: Trim around a picture frame
items.feedback: Trim runs along the edge — perimeter.

items.label: Paint to cover a wall
items.feedback: Paint covers the whole surface — area.

widget.missFeedback: Ask: does the job run ALONG the edge (perimeter) or COVER the inside (area)?
widget.successFeedback: Fencing and trim follow the edge (perimeter); carpet and paint fill the inside (area).

explanationVariants: Perimeter adds EVERY side, whatever the shape: 6 + 8 + 10 = 24 cm around the triangle.
A triangle has three sides — walk all three: 6 + 8 + 10 = 24.

widget.prompt: A triangle has sides of 6 cm, 8 cm, and 10 cm. What is its perimeter?

commonErrors.feedback: 48 multiplied 6 × 8 — an area reflex. Perimeter is a WALK: add every side, all three of them.
14 walked only two sides (6 + 8). The 10-cm side completes the loop: 6 + 8 + 10 = 24.

hints: Fencing follows the edge — that's perimeter.
A rectangle has two lengths and two widths.
explanationVariants: Two 12s and two 5s: 12 + 5 + 12 + 5 = 34 m of fencing.

widget.prompt: A rectangular garden is 12 m long and 5 m wide. How many meters of fencing enclose it?

commonErrors.feedback: 60 is 12 × 5 — the AREA of soil inside. Fencing follows the edge: add all four sides for 34.
17 walked only two sides (12 + 5). The fence needs both pairs: 12 + 5 + 12 + 5 = 34.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Add all four sides, or double (12 + 5).

takeaways: Perimeter = the distance all the way around — add every side.
Rectangle: two lengths + two widths, or double (length + width).
Square: 4 × side. Perimeter is the edge; area is the inside.
steps.teaser: next: the fence is known, but one side is missing — find it.

concept.body: Quick rewind. Perimeter is an **ant's walk around the edge** — start at one corner, follow every side back to the start, and add up all the distance walked. Miss a side and the ant falls off; walk them ALL.

explanationVariants: All four sides of a 5-cm square: 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20 cm.

widget.prompt: A square has 5 cm sides. Its perimeter is…

options.label: 10 cm
options.feedback: 10 walked only two sides. A square has FOUR: 5 × 4 = 20.

options.label: 25 cm
options.feedback: 25 is 5 × 5 — the area inside. The fence around is 4 × 5 = 20.
